attributes.title: render_trend_chart
attributes.description: Renders a real trend chart (stacked line panels with each tag's alarm setpoints, a first-deviation marker and the trip marker) for a stored alarm flood event, and returns the Markdown image reference to embed in the report plus per-tag facts: baseline, peak, and time of first deviation. Use this for the trend/history evidence section INSTEAD of printing a table of raw history samples -- an onset is visible on a chart and invisible in a column of numbers. By default the view auto-focuses on the measured ramp, which matters because a fault can develop in seconds inside a ten-minute event window.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: The flood event's event_id to chart. Get it from query_alarm_flood_events first; never guess it.

parameters.name: tag_paths
parameters.description: Optional comma-separated or JSON-array list of tag paths to plot. Omit to use the earliest-firing historised tags in the event, which is normally the right choice for root-cause work. Plot at most 6-8 tags or the panels get too short to read.

parameters.name: full_window
parameters.description: Set true to plot the entire stored event window including the hold period. Default false auto-focuses the view on the measured ramp so a fast fault is legible.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Chart width in pixels, 480-1600. Defaults to 720, which matches the report pane width -- leave it unset unless the user asks for a wider chart.
